text:
On the evening of 14 October 1987, the lamp at Sennet Point burned as it had on every night since 1875, and then it did not. Harbourmaster Idris Calloway of the Sennet Point Port Authority signed the final order and recorded the shutdown himself, a plain entry closing 112 years of continuous operation.

The decision rested on Port Authority Decommissioning Notice No. 87-31, issued ahead of the automated Corran Buoy beacon taking over the station's navigation duties. A machine anchored offshore would now do what keepers had once done by hand, season after season, through fog and gale.

The lighthouse was decommissioned in 1987. Those who remember the beam sweeping the harbour mouth speak less of the technology than of its constancy. For more than a century, the light had simply been there, and then its absence became the new fact of the coast.
